summary: Slovakia's police statistics give offenders by citizenship only for broad crime groups (sexual, violent), and child victims by age, sex and relationship to the offender without citizenship. The Interior Ministry's trafficking report gives victims and accused by citizenship. No crime statistic records ethnicity or Roma identity.

nations.National (Interior Ministry, Prosecutor: Monthly police crime statistics; trafficking situation report; prosecution yearbook.

european_title: Not recorded by any Slovak crime source
european_note: Slovak crime statistics separate only foreign citizens from Slovak citizens. The census records nationality (including Roma and Hungarians), but no crime, victim or child-protection statistic does, so neither European descent nor Roma identity can be measured for child harm.
proxy_note: Slovakia records citizenship only in crime data, never ethnicity or nationality. Every group below is a proxy, not ethnicity.

harms.label: Sexual (mravnostná) crime group (all victims)
harms.intro: Of 619 cleared sexual offences in 2025, 24 were committed by foreign citizens. Citizenship is published only by crime group, never for child sexual abuse itself. Child victims are published by section with age and sex but no citizenship.

perpetrators.scope: Slovakia, cleared sexual (mravnostná) offences, all victims, 2025

Citizenship, a proxy, not ethnicity: foreign citizens are people without Slovak citizenship (most often Ukrainian, Czech, Hungarian and Polish); Slovak citizens include Roma, Hungarians and every other nationality group.

harms.label: Trafficking in human beings (identified victims and accused)
harms.intro: The Interior Ministry's 2024 situation report counts 43 identified trafficking victims, 23 of them children; the only foreign victims were 3 adult Bulgarian men, so all child victims were Slovak citizens. Of 22 people accused of trafficking, 21 were Slovak citizens and 1 Turkish. For 2025 the ministry reported 63 victims (27 children), almost a quarter foreign, without a child-by-citizenship split.

breakdown.why: The Interior Ministry's 2025 crime statistics (table 6) give cleared offences by the perpetrator's citizenship only by crime group: 24 of 619 cleared sexual ('mravnostná') offences were committed by foreign citizens, all victim ages. Table 5 gives child victims (under 18) per section of the Criminal Code with age, sex and the offender's relationship, but no citizenship.
135 of 3,430 cleared violent offences in 2025 were committed by foreign citizens, all victim ages. Child victims of violence have no citizenship.
Neglect offences are not shown separately in the citizenship table (only 'other' and 'remaining' crime groups). Child victims have no citizenship.
Murders are inside the violent-crime group of the citizenship table (135 of 3,430 cleared violent offences by foreigners). No victims by citizenship.

The Interior Ministry's trafficking situation report (2024) gives 43 identified victims (23 children); the only foreign victims were 3 adult Bulgarians, and 21 accused traffickers were Slovak citizens and 1 Turkish. For 2025 the ministry reported 63 victims (27 children), almost a quarter foreign, without a child-by-citizenship split.
Child pornography falls in the sexual ('mravnostná') group of the citizenship table (24 of 619 by foreigners). No victims by citizenship.

components.name: Victim heritage
components.full: Official data by harm that separately identify children of European descent (e.g. White non-Hispanic, White British) alongside every other group, self-reported or official, few unknowns. Broad categories that lump European-descent people with others get partial credit; proxies (nationality, citizenship, migration background, country of birth) at most 9.4 points.

components.name: Perpetrator heritage
components.full: Same standard for perpetrators: not perceived, few unknowns, European descent separately identified. Proxies at most 9.4 points.

components.name: Coverage and missing data
components.full: Over 90% of the population covered, under 10% unknown

components.name: Rates and linkage
components.full: Rates per 100,000 possible, and victim heritage linked to perpetrator heritage

score.gold_standard: 100% means a country publishes data that separately identifies people of European descent, both as perpetrators (so one can tell when they disproportionately harm a group) and as child victims (so one can tell when European-descent children are disproportionately harmed), alongside every other group, linked victim to perpetrator, for every harm.
score.rules: Heritage is 75 of every 100 points (victims 37.5, perpetrators 37.5); coverage, rates and access share the other 25. Proxies such as nationality or migration background earn at most a quarter of the heritage points. A country with no real ethnicity data for victims or perpetrators is capped at 25%.
score.why: Slovakia scores 11% on the stricter scale (0-20%). Police statistics give offenders by citizenship only for broad crime groups (sexual, violent), child victims without citizenship, and trafficking victims and accused by citizenship in the Interior Ministry's report. No ethnicity is recorded.
score.weights_id: harm weights of 19 Nov 2026 (homicide 25, sexual abuse 20, sex trafficking 20, physical abuse 15, online exploitation 10, neglect 10)
